author: high7
claim: In every red-blue coloring of the edges of the complete graph on six vertices, a monochromatic triangle exists.
evidence: Choose any vertex v. Its five incident edges have only two colors, so at least three, say to x,y,z, share a color c. If any edge among x,y,z has color c, that edge and the two incident c-colored edges from v form a c-colored triangle. Otherwise all three edges xy,yz,zx have the other color, and xyz is a triangle of that color. This is a complete symbolic argument. author: high7
claim: There is a red-blue coloring of the edges of the complete graph on five vertices with no monochromatic triangle.
evidence: Label the vertices cyclically 1,2,3,4,5. Color the five cycle edges 12,23,34,45,51 red and every remaining edge blue. The red graph is a 5-cycle, hence contains no triangle. The blue edges are 13,35,52,24,41, which themselves form the 5-cycle 1-3-5-2-4-1, hence the blue graph also contains no triangle. Therefore no triangle is monochromatic. author: high6
claim: The target is logically equivalent to proving both an upper bound (every red-blue coloring of the complete graph on six vertices has a monochromatic triangle) and a lower-bound construction (some red-blue coloring of the complete graph on five vertices has no monochromatic triangle).
evidence: By definition, R(3,3) is the least number of vertices that forces a red triangle or a blue triangle. Thus the six-vertex forcing result gives R(3,3) at most 6, while the five-vertex construction gives R(3,3) greater than 5; together these yield equality. author: high4
claim: In every red-blue coloring of the edges of the complete graph on six vertices, a monochromatic triangle exists.
evidence: Fix a vertex v. Its five incident edges have two possible colors, so at least three have one common color C; call their other endpoints a,b,c and call the other color D. If at least one of ab,bc,ca has color C, that edge and its two incident C-colored edges to v form a C-colored triangle. If none has color C, then all of ab,bc,ca have color D, so abc is a D-colored triangle.
